        How to read it
        • Up is time. … at the bottom, … at the top.
        • Out from the centre is distance from the root person. Their line is the bright trunk; one ring out is a parent or child of someone on it.
        • Around is which family. Every branch owns a wedge of the circle; T looks straight down on them.
        • Colour is where they were born, or whatever you pick above.
        • Clicking someone dims the rest to their own line. F turns that off.

        Click any point to see who it is. ? lists every key.

        What to open next

          Ancestors

          Two things about this line's own ancestry that a pedigree chart cannot draw, because a pedigree chart shows every ancestor exactly once and in a real family neither of those assumptions holds.

          Load-bearing ancestors

          Every path up to these people goes through one person. Remove them and everyone behind them stops being an ancestor at all — not because the records run out, but because that is how the descent runs. The number is how many ancestors go with them. Click to see who.

            Reached by two lines

            Ancestors this line reaches more than once. Click one to draw its lines.

              Where they went

              Every dated event in the tree that could be put on a map — … of them, for … people. A line is drawn when one person's next recorded place is a different one, so what you are watching is the family moving, not a summary of it.

              Key
              The record names a town a county a state only a country

              What the records say

              One finding per card: the title is what the records show, the line under it is what was measured.
